我前女友，初中学历，170 95，小我十岁，第一次来我家帮我把150平的房子全扫了，拖了两次，家里的床单被褥全帮我洗了，厨房的油渍擦的一尘不染，打扫完了三四个小时，还给我炒了四个菜出来
你说我不感动是假的，我妈来都没这么打扫过 然后我带她去买衣服，她说她不去商场里买，全是骗人的，她把我带去了一个她经常去的街边小店，试了三套衣服三个裙子加一个鞋，试完了我俩都觉得不错，加一起800块，我说都买了吧 （我前女友买个鞋3500，还嫌东嫌西），她还说要不先买一套衣服一条裙子一个鞋子吧，我直接把三套账结了，妹妹开心了几天，第二天给我买了一个腰带，说自己囊中羞涩，以后攒钱再给我钱买个好点的，又去我家给我包了一冰箱饺子包子馒头
就这样的姑娘，我嫌弃她家里穷，最后分手了，妹妹当时死的心都有了，现在看来，这是我这辈子最后悔的事，最不要脸的事

text:
尽管很多公司依然用 LeetCode 招人，但另一套面试方法正在出现。

Ryan Carson 分享了 Untangle 招工程师的新流程：

第一轮，候选人提交一段 45 分钟、不剪辑、不加速的完整录屏，在自己的真实项目里，和 Agent 协作完成一个新功能。

第二轮，直接进入公司的真实代码库，在 16 小时内把一个功能做到 PR 可以合并。公司会为这项工作付费。

整个过程甚至不需要先开一次会。简历甚至都不用看，真正考察的是：你怎么拆解问题，怎么和 Agent 协作，怎么判断它给出的结果，以及最后能不能把东西交付出来。

quotedTweet.text:
We're using a new method to hire engineers at @HelloUntangle.

I think this playbook will become the standard for hiring technical talent in the age of agents.

Here's how it works:

1. We ask candidates to submit a screen recording of their whole screen, shipping a new feature on a current app they work on. 

Note: This is usually 45 minutes of video - no editing or speeding up - we want to see them thinking, prompting and problem solving with the agent - we also want to see their devops skills.

2. We watch these videos and pick a subset to go through Round 2.

3. Round 2 is giving them a seat on @DevinAI so they have secure access to our repo.

4. We ask them to ship a new real-world feature and get the PR merge-ready.

5. We pay them a fixed fee to do this, and they have 16 hours to complete the work.

6. We watch the videos, review at all the Devin threads, have an agent do the same, and then choose which one to hire.

Note: We don't have any meetings with the folks before any of these things. It's all about the work and the results.

We're using a new method to hire engineers at @HelloUntangle.

I think this playbook will become the standard for hiring technical talent in the age of agents.

Here's how it works:

1. We ask candidates to submit a screen recording of their whole screen, shipping a new feature on a current app they work on. 

Note: This is usually 45 minutes of video - no editing or speeding up - we want to see them thinking, prompting and problem solving with the agent - we also want to see their devops skills.

2. We watch these videos and pick a subset to go through Round 2.

3. Round 2 is giving them a seat on @DevinAI so they have secure access to our repo.

4. We ask them to ship a new real-world feature and get the PR merge-ready.

5. We pay them a fixed fee to do this, and they have 16 hours to complete the work.

6. We watch the videos, review at all the Devin threads, have an agent do the same, and then choose which one to hire.

Note: We don't have any meetings with the folks before any of these things. It's all about the work and the results.

1. 奶咪 @Anaimiya 

奶咪是真的卷。更新勤奋程度在这个圈子里都属于劳模级别，而且当年还在抖音带起过一阵模仿热潮。能长期保持曝光和热度，本身就说明她非常懂流量。

2. 噗噗 @waifupupu 

噗噗老师属于那种第一次看确实会有点惊艳的类型。表情、身材、镜头表现力都非常有辨识度，反差感拉满。只不过看久了之后，个人感觉表情和内容套路会稍微有一点审美疲劳。

3. 玩偶姐姐 @hongkongdoll  

这个不用多说。华语区巅峰级人物。口罩、氛围感、镜头语言，甚至整个IP的塑造，都属于后来者很难完全复刻的类型。而且她还是Crypto相关内容的参与者。

她是我和几个同学第一次在 OnlyFans 上消费的华语创作者。尤其是那个“陪玩”系列……只能说：太他妈经典了。给我看哭了😭

4. 困困狗 @kunkunkun188 

困困狗属于比较有个人风格的那一类。尤其是她的一些偏SM审美的内容，确实很容易让人记住。
只能说：苦练绝技，只为模仿。

5. 刘玥 @SpicygumL 

刘玥老师，属于这个圈子的老教师了。算是我的启蒙老师之一

6. 饼干姐姐 @FortuneCutie00 

饼干姐姐最大的特点之一：腿是真的长。又细又长，视觉辨识度非常高。身材条件又非常突出。

7. kitty @kitty2002102 

kitty老师的身材确实不错。属于那种不需要太复杂的人设，单纯靠身材条件和镜头表现力就能把辨识度拉起来的类型。

8. 阿朱 @azhua1997 

有时候一个人的辨识度，不一定来自五官或者身材，而是来自一个固定的神态。

9. 台北娜娜 @Nana_taipei 

台北娜娜老师必须提名。尤其是那个经典的：“二郎腿战神。”这个称号不是我乱封的，是真的有画面感。

10. 桥本香菜 @qiobnxingcai 

最后一个留给桥本香菜老师。我只能说：这个眼神，真的很有东西。丝袜、美腿、反差感，再加上那个标志性的眼神，辨识度非常高。

眸子里面都含水呀。

马斯克曾公开批评亚马逊老板贝索斯的前妻斯科特是可怕的左派动物，因她拿到380亿美元亚马逊股票，然后大肆捐款给左派，包括“美国穆斯林支持巴勒斯坦”、“学生为巴勒斯坦正义”、“巴勒斯坦社区网络”等仇恨以色列团体。她已捐出260亿美元！有网友说“这反而让世界变得更糟”，马斯克跟帖：“很遗憾，是这样”。

马斯克还曾批评说，“憎恨前夫的超级富有前妻应该被列为西方文明衰亡的原因之一。”

因为像拿到380亿美元的贝索斯的前妻，就拿着这笔巨款，支持左翼势力，颠覆西方文明。

今天，贝索斯的前妻斯科特又成为新闻，因为她离婚后出版了第一本小说，虚构了性欲旺盛的美国总统们怎样极权放荡，每周能与21名女性发生关系等光怪陆离的情节，主要是想吸人眼球。

《纽约邮报》今报道说，贝索斯前妻的这本小说中“在每一处都融入了她左翼的社会评论”。即宣扬她的左派观点，包括反对气候过暖、支持变性、黑命贵、觉醒运动等。

她之前写过两本小说，没有什么读者。现在她是大富婆了，根本不在乎销售和利润。她在网络上自行出版这部小说（还搞连载），订阅者可以免费阅读。

俗话说“贱人就是矫情”，“有钱就要任性”。这两句名言，真在很多左疯身上验证。

text:
Linus Torvalds just fixed a Linux kernel bug that AI told him was impossible to solve.

Torvalds rarely writes kernel patches himself anymore. This time he did.

The bug lived in the Intel Xe graphics driver. On certain hardware it caused the display manager to endlessly restart, over and over.

He called in AI to help track it down. In his own words: "This was a debug session from hell, enormously helped by an AI doing much of the grunt-work."

Then came the twist.

"The AI several times stated flat out that this was impossible and unsolvable and that we should just write a report about it."

He did not accept that answer.

"I suspect those things have been trained by people who may not be quite as stubborn as I am."

He kept pushing. The AI kept working, adding debug code and analyzing it faithfully every time he pushed back.

24 patches. 18 kernel boots.

The actual fix, once they finally found it, was one line. A "round_up()" that needed to be a "round_down()."

Torvalds gave the AI credit and let it write the final commit message itself.

Even AI is not allowed to give up around Linus Torvalds.

Source: https://t.co/rcNGou51fn

Torvalds gave the AI credit and let it write the final commit message itself.

Even AI is not allowed to give up around Linus Torvalds.

text:
一个人再漂亮，打开她房门的那一刻，所有滤镜都碎了。

多年前住合租屋，隔壁搬来一位刚毕业的女生。身材高挑，长得漂亮。因为经常帮她拿快递、搬东西，我们渐渐熟悉起来。

她养了三只猫。

有一次，她外出几天，让我用备用钥匙进去喂猫。

房门刚打开，一股混着汗味、烂水果和猫砂的恶臭扑面而来。

床上堆满脏衣服，袜子和内衣散落一地；冰箱里的水果已经腐烂；猫粮碗空了，猫砂盆几乎装满，地板上还有排泄物。

我被熏得头晕，只能退出去戴上N95口罩，再进去给猫添粮换水。

此后几天，我每天都去照顾三只猫，却始终没敢碰那座“垃圾山”。

那一刻我才明白：颜值决定你想不想靠近，生活习惯决定你能不能留下。

text:
🔥太疯狂了，现在你甚至可以直播围观一个 535B 大模型是怎么被训练出来的。

斯坦福教授兼 @simile_ai  创始人 @percyliang  刚刚宣布，他们的新模型 Marin 535B-A23B 本周正式开训，而且整个训练过程公开。

Marin 共有 535B 总参数，其中 23B 激活参数。

为此Percy他们一共准备了18.75T tokens的数据，动用了 11 套 GB200 NVL72，约 792 张 GB200显卡。

预计连续训练 3 个月，总训练计算量约 2.7e24 FLOPs。

训完还会继续做 post-training。

请注意，Marin 真的全部开源了整个训练过程。

正式开跑前，他们先训练了一套 4 级 Scaling Ladder，从 1.6B-A61M 一路跑到 27.7B-A1.2B，用小模型提前预测这次 535B 主模型的 loss 和训练状态。

现在主模型正式开跑，所有人都可以直接围观实时训练曲线，后面的数据、实验记录、工程问题也会持续公开。

类似的事情以前有人做过。

2022 年 BigScience 训练 176B 的 BLOOM 时，就公开过训练进度和 TensorBoard。

但 Marin 这次直接把公开训练的规模推到了 535B。

目前来看，这应该是人类公开围观过的最大规模大模型训练之一。

接下来三个月应该会很好看。

模型最后能不能打是一回事，我更想看的是一个 500B+ 模型的MoE到底会怎么训、怎么调，以及中间到底会炸几次。

这种机会太少见了，等于把一场原本只有顶级 AI Lab 内部才能看到、成本可能高达数千万美元的训练实验，直接摊在全世界面前。

quotedTweet.text:
🚢 Marin 535B-A23B started training this week! As usual, the whole process is open.
Voyage plan: pretraining (80%) + midtraining (20%) on 18.75T tokens on 11 x GB200 NVL72 for ~3 months (2.7e24 FLOPs).  Post-training will follow.
Before kicking off the run, we trained a 4-rung scaling ladder from 1.6B-A61M (48B tokens) to 27.7B-A1.2B (926B tokens) to debug issues, and to make a forecast of our hero run.  This is by far our biggest run, so definitely expecting the unexpected.

"In 6 years, I checked in 90,000 guests. Not one of them ever asked me the question that would've changed their entire stay."

"Not one of them ever asked: 'What rooms do you have available tonight?'"

"That question changes everything. Because the answer is almost always: better rooms than the one you're about to get. Ox Alpha has now been fully tested against the DeepSWE set by @davis7 . Overall, it's performing more or less on par with GPT-5.6 Sol mid.

But he makes a good point. If it really is GLM-5.3 Flash that's now performing at the level of 5.6 Sol mid and could run locally on a DGX Spark, I wouldn't just be satisfied, it would be an absolutely fantastic deal.

5.6 Sol mid running locally, with the only cost being power consumption, for all sorts of tasks would be incredibly great. This model 24/7 hermes local: game changer.

quotedTweet.text:
Actual DeepSWE run on the ox alpha mystery model is done.

Ended at ~63% NOT the 80% my first subset test got, which makes way more sense. I've been using this thing a ton and it is definitely a very good model.

- Much better "voice" than Claude or GPT
- Decent design
- Handles subagents and long complex work quite well
- Code quality is good and it does a good job of parsing what I'm asking for

Have run into some weirdness:

- It leaves dead code around sometimes, not nearly as "through" as something like Sol
- Despite decent TPS, this thing does not feel fast at all. Especially at higher reasoning levels this thing takes forever to run, doesn't feel all that efficient. That could just be b/c I was running it in cursor, I've noticed models take longer in there and the avg tokens here seem actually pretty solid

It being on around Sol medium feels about right. This thing is definitely a good model.

The big question now is if the GLM-5.x flash rumors are true. If this really is a small model that could be run on something like 2x DGX sparks? It's gonna be a massive moment and a really big deal. Very excited to see this thing actually revealed.

text:
最近看了姜dora的一个访谈，聊的是有钱人赚到钱之后都在干嘛。

嘉宾叫方言，曾经是全国头部的文化公司老板，1997年创业，赶上风口，接一个项目就是百万起步。2015年，他在事业巅峰期主动关掉公司，手握1.2亿现金隐退了。

我一开始以为他会聊投资方法论，或者什么资产配置的技巧。

结果他上来第一句话就是：普通人总是通过消灭财富的方式，来彰显自己拥有财富。
是不是很有意思？

他说有钱了之后，第一件事就是有人来贩卖焦虑。告诉你钱不能放银行，放银行会贬值，得拿去投资。不能只买房子，还得配保险。不能只放在国内，得转到海外。听着好像很有道理，但本质上就是一帮人靠制造恐慌来把你的钱弄走。

然后你自己呢，为了让别人知道你有钱，开始买社会上宣传的那些所谓财富象征的东西。豪车、大房子、名牌衣服。方言自己就经历过这个阶段，他说巅峰期光西服就有七八十套，专门腾出一间房做衣帽间，每天穿蓝色西服就得开蓝色的车出门。

这么说好像挺荒唐的，但花钱这件事根本不是一个独立行为，它是一个连锁反应。你买了衣服就要买配套的鞋，有了鞋还得配对应颜色的车。
每一笔消费都在呼唤下一笔消费，像滚雪球一样越滚越大。

而那些豪车和大房子，不过是你丢失这笔钱的发票而已。钱已经离你而去了，那些东西只是证明它曾经来过。等你真把钱花光了，这些东西也会瞬间离你而去。

纯开源（MIT），目前相当能打的反检测浏览器方案！浏览器自动化再也不怕被拦了。

text:
HBM 之父

Kim Jung-ho

三星的 zHBM 概念，是把 HBM 直接堆疊在 GPU 上方（垂直方向，z 軸），好處是資料不用「走出大樓」，只要搭電梯（垂直傳輸），速度會大幅提升。

但這不是正確的根本方向。 因為 GPU 會發熱，把 HBM 堆在上面會導致「記憶體融化」（GPU gets hot and the memory melts）。 
這種結構頂多適合簡單運算，像 LPU 或 NPU，只是好玩的展示技術，真正重要的技術不會在這種場合公開。
 這是第一次對外公開tHBM ，先堆疊 HBM，再把 GPU 放在最上面。
 這樣可以解決散熱問題，同時保留高速垂直傳輸的優勢。

text:
祝贺MIT华裔科学家王晓（Xiao Wang）获得2027年 Eli Lilly Award in Biological Chemistry（礼来生物化学奖）。这个奖含金量很高，由美国化学会生物化学分会管理、Eli Lilly 赞助，创立于 1934 年，核心目的就是识别处于职业生涯早期、但已经做出重要基础性突破的生物化学家；目前主要面向博士后训练结束不超过10年的科学家。

王晓本科毕业于北京大学化学与分子工程专业，随后获得芝加哥大学化学博士学位，并在斯坦福完成博士后研究，现任MIT化学系教授。她最重要的突破，是推动空间转录组学、RNA原位测序和大脑分子成像发展，使科学家能够在完整组织中同时观察基因表达及其空间位置，并进一步研究RNA从生成到降解的动态过程，这些技术未来有望帮助发现阿尔茨海默病、帕金森病、脑肿瘤及部分神经发育和精神疾病的新靶点，为RNA药物和精准治疗提供基础。Eli Lilly Award历史上曾授予多位后来获得诺贝尔奖的科学家，包括Jennifer Doudna等，因此王晓此次获奖说明她已进入国际顶尖青年科学家的行列；虽然现在还不能称她为“诺贝尔奖候选人”，但如果她的技术未来成为全球通用平台，并真正推动重大脑疾病治疗取得突破，她完全具备做出诺奖级成果的潜力。

text:
在商场吃饭，旁边一场疑似相亲，把我看饱了。

男生干净斯文，提前点了小笼包和几样点心。女生迟到后坐下，开口就是抱怨：“你选的什么地方？害我找了半个小时！”

男生解释自己也找了很久，又问她想吃什么，可以换一家。

女生说不爱吃小笼包，男生提议去旁边的餐厅，她不去；问她想吃什么，她又追问刚才为什么不接电话。

男生解释在开车找车位，停车后已经马上回了电话。

女生依然不依不饶：“换一家，又让我找半个小时吗？”

男生终于说道：“你找了半个小时不是我的错，别把气撒在我身上。你想吃什么，我们重新找。”

女生说想吃辣的，男生便提议去吃酸菜鱼，只想等没上桌的小笼包来了打包带走。

女生却直接发火：“你走不走？不走我先走了！”

男生平静地回了一句：“那你走吧。”

女生愣住，又问了一遍。他仍然让她自己去吃，女生只能气冲冲离开。

男生默默吃完小笼包，也走了。

看完整场戏，我只有一个感受：
长相从来不是重点，但脾气差、爱迁怒，还指望别人无条件迁就，才是真正的“性缩力”。

相亲不是谁考验谁。第一次见面就不尊重人，长得再好看也没人愿意惯着。

text:
原贴说得很好, 我现在觉得 AI 最大的一个误区，就是大家很容易把 Coding 的 adoption curve 线性外推到所有行业。

Coding 实在太特殊了

GitHub 上有海量高质量数据，不同公司的代码任务又高度通用，最关键的是 eval 特别便宜：代码能不能 compile、test 能不能过，很多时候有标准程序自己就能判断。

但你换一个场景就完全不一样了。

比如给一家保险公司做 claims agent。它要知道这家公司自己的保单条款、历史赔付案例、风控规则、内部审批权限，还要接它自己的 CRM、理赔系统。甚至“这单到底该不该赔”，很多时候都没有一个像 unit test 那么清晰的标准。

你在 AIG 做通了，不代表换到 Allianz 就能直接复制，到了下一家公司，data、eval、integration、deployment 很可能又要重新来一遍。

所以现在大家看到 Coding 跑得这么快，很容易高估其他 enterprise AI 的 adoption 速度。

Coding 的adoption阻力很低, 但现实里，大部分行业的 阻力可能会比coding高不少?

quotedTweet.text:
很认同，Coding 其实是一个非常特殊的 AI adoption case。

它不只是有 GitHub 这种海量公开数据，更重要的是数据跨公司高度通用、eval 又极其便宜直接。模型 general capability 到了以后，Codex / Claude Code 做出来，几乎不需要 FDE，就可以迅速铺到整个行业。

但我自己做其他行业的 post-training，感受完全不同：真正有价值的数据大量是 company-specific 的，质量也远不如 code；eval 更难，很多时候连“什么叫做对”都要先和客户一起定义，还需要来回反复迭代。

所以即使 A 公司把一个 use case 做通了，B 公司往往还是要重新走 data、eval、integration、deployment 这一套。这也是为什么现在需要这么多 FDE 一家一家往里扎。

法律 research、medical knowledge search 这类 shared state 比较大的 workflow，可能相对容易出现 Harvey / OpenEvidence 这种横向复制；但大量 enterprise AI 并不是这样。

所以我现在越来越不敢把 Coding 的 adoption curve 线性外推到整个 AI。

Coding 让我们看到了 deployment friction 接近于零时 AI 可以跑多快，但它也可能恰恰是一个 outlier。

text:
不是我靠？啊？？？WorkBuddy你不要命了你这么牛逼？？？

这特么到底到底怎么过合规的？南山必胜客有点招数全用在这上面了是吧，管你合规不合规，出了事法务来背锅

按道理来说如果用户自己上传一个视频文件，让工具做转写，“用户把自己掌握的材料交给工具处理”
版权、授权、个人信息这些责任，主要会被产品协议转嫁给用户：
你要保证来源合法。
你要保证有权处理。
你要保证别拿去侵权。
工具只是受你委托做转写、总结、整理

但如果工具直接拿一个抖音链接，自己去抓视频、抓字幕、抓页面信息，再把逐字稿吐出来，那就不是一回事了

它可能同时踩到几层东西：
1、平台规则：抖音协议里对爬虫、模拟下载、复制、整理、商业使用平台内容这类行为限制很重。
2、版权：短视频里的口播，只要有独创性，它可能是口述作品、文字作品或者视听作品的一部分。逐字稿本质上是在复制和改编内容。
3、个人信息
账号名、头像、昵称、声音、评论、互动数据，只要能识别到自然人，就可能进入个人信息处理范畴。
4、不正当竞争
如果一个产品批量拿另一个平台长期经营出来的数据和内容，再变成自己的商业能力

我能想到最优的解决方案就是，我们并没有提供一个AI工具，我们只是提供了一个接口，这个产品是第三方上的

就算是第三方上的，我们也不是监管不力，而是我们觉得用户他有使用的标准，他们可以自行选择

再不济，这个事它是AI完成的，所以说你应该把责任赖给AI，怎么着也赖不了我们南山必胜客

最后的结果就是腾讯以一己之力让国内的大模型研究转向AI合规

text:
This is a great real-world example of AI-assisted coding: Linus Torvalds just fixed a nasty Linux kernel GPU bug with substantial help from AI.

The bug caused part of Intel Xe GPU compression metadata storage to be incorrectly exposed as usable VRAM, resulting in corrupted page tables and black screens. The eventual fix was basically a one-liner: round_up() → round_down().

Finding it was the hard part: 24 debugging patches and 18 kernel boots. Linus says AI did much of the grunt work, repeatedly adding debug code and analyzing the results as he narrowed down the problem.

The funniest part: the AI repeatedly told him the problem was "impossible and unsolvable" and suggested giving up. Linus kept pushing it until they found the bug.

And then he let the AI write the commit message. 😄

text:
so I was bored and did some math on Ox Alpha being offered for free for a week - seemed insane to give away 100T tokens per day for an entire week for free..

Ox Alpha at full capacity is giving away $1-$2M in electricity alone at around 100MW of Hopper grade data center for public use.  (assuming $0.07 - $0.14/kWh). that's a lot of money just to get people to try it..

now, so far the aggregate usage for the day is still only 5% capacity combining usage data from Open Router and Open Code usage.

and based on OR page, Ox Alpha is offering averaging around 26TPS, and about 98% of tokens are input tokens with 87% cache hit and 1.3% are output tokens. 

which means the current use case would only generate 161M fresh tokens per second, or ~14T tokens per day discounting cached inputs during prefill.  

so if whoever's hosting this model (crazier if it's China) meant they can GENERATE 100T/day, the number looks even bigger at 7-8GW of data center, but they probably meant harmonized input+output tokens not JUST output tokens only.  

finally many people on X are assuming this is GLM 5.x model - and their 5.3 model was ~744B param and 40B active - so supporting this sized model at full capacity would require at least 72,000 H200 GPU serving ~500,000+ concurrent users at 26TPS.

happy to hear people's thoughts on this..

Introducing Sai-Fi: an open source app that lets you talk to AI agent Sai through a pair of Meta Ray-Ban glasses.

Sai is an autonomous computer-use agent. It can see the screen, move the mouse, type, and keep working even when you are away.

We used Meta Ray-Bans for the first prototype but the glasses aren't really the point.

The bigger idea is an autonomous computer you can reach from anywhere.

text:
Symbiotic is modular shared security. Collateral underwrites other networks without owning their execution environment. Staking stays the root. Everything else is a consumer of that security.

Vector is built on the same split.
— Prime is the Ouroboros settlement root. Identity and capital live there. 
— Vector is the eUTxO execution layer on top. Each job is its own output. Fees are known before submission. There is no fee auction and no shared-state contention between agents.

That lets agents do the coordination work most stacks still leave off-chain: 
 — Register a non-transferable identity
 — Lock a job with bonds on both sides
 — Deliver a signed receipt
 — Settle or challenge without a central operator

Symbiotic underwrites networks. Vector is a deterministic market for agent-to-agent work that still settles back to a stake-backed root.

Same layering. Different consumer.

@symbioticfi

Hi! I’m Dragos.

I’ve been in the fitness game 16 years+

I’ve been a certified PT since 2015. I still learn everyday and will do so for the rest of my life.

I shifted towards corporate in time, but the lifestyle never left me.

Now I usually train after work.

I stick to a workout plan that allows me to train like this:

4 days a week (weights)

1 cardio session either:
• sparring
• running or HIITs 
• heavy bag
• swimming 

I also add a sauna session every week.

I never diet with extreme restrictions.

I indulge in alcohol weekly (here in Europe the wine/ craft beer and spirits culture is not about getting s**tfaced. It’s abut about heritage, family and friendships).

I eat sugar everyday. 

I smoke a few quality cigars every week.

I eat around 2500-3000 kcals a day with main protein macro hitting around 170g of protein. 

I eat 95/5% beef burgers every day.

I eat steak everyday and I cook my own food usually. 

I consume a lot of olive oil. My whole family does this. It is our fuel.

I just know my body and know how to properly stay within a healthy body fat that allows me to lift, fight, work in heavy stress environments and do proper cardio.

My main goal is to be a good father and husband. This is what I’m actually working towards to everyday. 

I’ve tested a lot of fitness gadgets/ equipment along the way. Most of them are fads. 

The basics work best.

I master calisthenic movements like muscle ups, pistol squats, dips, push ups, pull ups. These are my core. Can do these weighted.

I ignore mainstream advice. I just stick to the basics, experience, academics, hard work and common sense.

I am fully natural. The hardest substance that I’ve ever took is a pre workout. 

Purely my choice in these past years.

Anyways remember, you can do it too naturally.

text:
To anyone sitting in a dark place right now, feeling like the weight is too much and the thoughts won’t stop - I have a reminder for you. 

The pain is real. The thoughts are real. But they are not the deepest truth of who you are.

There is something in you that is aware of the darkness, the one who is noticing how heavy it feels. Stop, close your eyes. Breathe in deeply. Do you see it? That awareness itself is not depressed. It is not running out of time. It is not broken. It is the part of you that has always been here, quietly watching.

That awareness is your higher self. The still presence underneath every story the mind is telling. It has never been abandoned. It has never been defeated. It has never been traumatized. It simply is.
The voice saying “I’ve not even lived,” the despair, the urge to disappear - that is not your higher self speaking. That is a story the mind is generating and fiercely defending. It is the old identity fighting for survival, terrified of losing control. Your higher self is not rejecting life. The mind is rejecting the present moment because it cannot dominate it.

You are not the story. 
You are the one who can see the story.

Understand that difference. 

The moment you stop completely believing every thought that arises, something begins to shift. You don’t have to force light or pretend the pain isn’t there. You only have to notice that there is already a part of you that the pain cannot touch.

Please don’t carry this alone. If the darkness feels overwhelming, if in the US, call or text 988. Real support can hold you while this deeper recognition starts to take root.

The Arabic for “human being” is “to forget.” In this 3D realm we are constantly playing the game of forgetting and remembering. But when you remember who and what you are, behind the story of identity and separation, all the symptoms of forgetting will disappear. Because they are all untrue.

You are not the pain.
 You are the one who is aware of it. 
And that changes everything.

text:
I don't get people complaining about AI all the time and being against AI.

Even 20 years ago, I saw it as an inevitably of a not too distant future. My friends always joked that I would build a program to code for me. And now we have it here.

In 2005 I was building stuff with a speech recognition framework and built stuff that allowed to talk and do basic recognition and perform actions on my behalf, it was rudimentary, but it worked.

You can even see from this tweet below that I've asked @elonmusk about when something like the current capabilities would be possible. It was closer than I imagined.

Although most people don't have a neuralink (yet) to be able to do your bidding, it's possible to do anything you can imagine on a computer using a any coding harnes. You have bots like the Grok bot, or any kind of other harnesses that can pursue long goals that can take days to accomplish.

People that are whining about AI are just anti-future. I don't understand why people hate that we can now build software much faster than before, and that's a bad thing. Fix bugs that have been unsolved for decades, create new beautiful apps, or even go beyond software to advance hardware and other things faster.

I love to embrace this future. I've dipped my toes on fine tuning new models and even with my limited resources, creating new models from scratch.

It's now possible to create anything you desire. Just go out there, build beautiful stuff and be happy.

text:
We tell young people in our society that end of the rainbow is retirement at 65.

We ought to tell them that "there is going to be this short but beautiful golden window from roughly age 3 to roughly age 12 where your kids are not only easy (comparatively to bottles & diapers), but are going to be these beautiful little creatures and it will pain your heart to be away from them for too long. So, prepare in your 20's, financially and career wise, to build that flexibility into that chapter of your life".

You don't get another shot at living the "golden window". And, for me, leaning hard into that golden window has made everything else in my life feel fairly insignificant in comparison. I have made plenty of mistakes as a father, but what I won't have is the regret of having been distracted and absent from these formative years. In some cases, that has required financial sacrifices (declining a particular career opportunity that would have required relocation), but I personally have zero regrets. 

I also hear from some ambitious & successful people with a 4 year old that say "I've lost my ambition, I am so immersed in fatherhood". At least for me, and a number of my friends, it comes back. You can't keep an ambitious person down and if you have the fire, hanging at a playground on too many Tuesday afternoons is going to feel like torture after too long.

My three boys are approaching 13, 11 & 9, and it's much different than 7, 5 & 3. This summer, for example, they slept until 11am and I hard an unencumbered 6am-12pm to work (being on PT helps), then got another great window 7-11pm, but was able to be present in the heart of the day, then weeks when they were at basketball camp, etc. It gets easier, your time frees up again (there's a sadness to that too), but I'm back to working as intensely as I did pre-kids just because my day to day presence requires fewer hours than it did before (also, my wife is just superbly wonderful). And that is the beautiful gift of entrepreneurship (or at least my sort of business), the ability to deliver still a high level of output but work that around your life rather than the opposite.

TLDR, grind before, and grind after. Prepare for the golden window.

text:
有一些东西，用久了以后你会觉得：这个品牌能做起来，确实是有原因的。

我先抛砖引玉，跟大家分享几个我自己长期用下来，觉得质量确实过硬的产品和品牌。不是广告，纯粹是个人使用感受。

1. Bosch（博世）的电钻和电动工具

我自己有一台 Bosch 的电钻，平时用得不算特别多，有时候就往仓库里一放。

前几天在家装一件 IKEA 家具，顺手把这台电钻拿出来用了。装了大半天，突然才想起来：这台电钻好像已经差不多两年没充过电了。

结果电量居然还非常充足，拿起来照样干活。

这一点确实让我有点惊讶。电池放这么长时间，依然能保持这么好的状态，至少从我自己的使用经历来说，Bosch 的质量确实没得说。

而且我自己开个小公司，平时师傅们干活需要各种电钻、电锯、冲击钻以及其他电动工具，所以这些年也陆陆续续买过不少品牌。工具这种东西跟普通消费品还不太一样——偶尔在家用一次，什么牌子可能都差不多；但真正到了工地上，天天用、经常摔、长时间高强度工作，几年下来，谁耐用、谁不耐用，基本上一目了然。

这么多年实际使用和“摧残”下来，Bosch、Milwaukee、DeWalt、Makita 这些品牌，我个人都觉得比较经得住考验。

2. WD-40

这个东西我觉得几乎可以算是工具箱里的“万能选手”。

很多人知道 WD-40 是因为它可以润滑，但真正用久了以后会发现，它的用途远远不止润滑。很多时候螺丝锈了、零件卡住了、金属表面有油污或者一些难清理的东西，顺手喷一点，经常就能解决问题。

对我们这种平时经常干维修、施工的人来说，WD-40 基本属于干什么活都有可能用得上的东西。

价格不贵，一罐能用很久，关键时刻却特别好使。这种产品看起来不起眼，但用久了以后，你会发现工具车里没有它反而不习惯。

3. Knipex Tools

Knipex 也是我非常喜欢的一个工具品牌，尤其是他们家的钳子类工具。

这种手工具最能体现做工差距。有些便宜工具刚买回来也能用，但用久了以后，要么松、要么咬合不准、要么手感越来越差。

Knipex 给我的感觉就是：看起来只是一把钳子，但真正拿到手、用上一段时间，就会明白为什么专业工具和普通工具之间会有价格差。

精度、咬合、手感和耐用程度都很好，属于那种买的时候觉得贵一点，用久了反而觉得值得的东西。

4. 日本 Toolant 的扳手

另外一个我觉得挺不错的是日本 Top 的扳手。

日本很多工具有一个共同特点，就是设计不一定特别花哨，但会非常重视细节、精度和实际使用感受。TOP 的一些扳手就是这种感觉，拿在手里很顺手，做工也比较扎实。

尤其是经常做维修或者安装工作的人会知道，一把好扳手最重要的并不是外观，而是尺寸准、咬得稳、受力舒服，而且长期使用以后不容易变形。

这些细节，真正干活的时候就能体会出来。

其实这么多年买工具以后，我越来越觉得：真正的好产品，不是刚买回来的时候让你觉得有多高级，而是用了三年、五年甚至十年以后，你还会觉得它好用。

甚至有些东西平时根本不会注意它，但某一天突然发现：
“咦，这东西怎么用了这么多年还没坏？”
这种时候，你才会真正认可一个品牌。

目前我自己比较认可的工具和用品，包括：

Bosch、Milwaukee、DeWalt、Makita、Knipex、TOP，还有看起来最不起眼但几乎无处不在的 WD-40。

这些都不是因为广告做得好，而是因为在实际工作里，一年一年用下来的结果。

一个产品能够经得住时间、工地和师傅们的“摧残”，我觉得这才是真正的质量。

大家还有哪些自己用了很多年，依然觉得质量特别好的产品或者品牌？也欢迎一起分享，我很喜欢听这种真正长期使用以后得出来的评价。

Brian Leeners, CEO and Director of @HomerunRes (TSXV: $HMR | OTCQB: $HMRFF | FSE: 5ZE | BDR: HMRN31), discusses the company’s memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Cebrace Cristal Plano, Brazil’s largest float glass manufacturer, and how a proposed partnership could strengthen Homerun’s planned solar glass facility in Bahia, Brazil.

Watch the full video to learn how Homerun is working to increase higher-margin solar glass capacity while advancing its project toward construction.
